jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is building the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The Site Readiness & Development team is responsible for translating OpenAI’s long-term infrastructure needs into executable data center capacity across self-build campuses, leased facilities, and strategic development partnerships. The team works across capacity planning, power, land, real estate, design, construction, finance, and commercial execution to ensure the right infrastructure is available in the right locations and on the timelines required to support OpenAI’s growth. About the Role We are seeking a Development Planner to own portfolio-level planning for future data center shell capacity. This role will translate compute-demand forecasts, power availability, technical requirements, and development schedules into a clear strategy for where, when, and how much shell capacity OpenAI should secure or build. You will evaluate capacity across self-build, lease, colocation, and development-partner pathways; identify future supply gaps; recommend campus and building phasing; and maintain the integrated plan connecting site readiness to construction, commissioning, and operational handoff. This is an individual contributor lead role requiring strong analytical judgment, infrastructure-development fluency, and the ability to drive decisions across teams without relying on formal authority. Key Responsibilities - Develop and maintain a multi-year portfolio plan for data center shell capacity across priority geographies. - Translate compute forecasts, IT-load requirements, rack-density assumptions, power schedules, cooling requirements, and deployment timelines into site and building requirements. - Determine when shell capacity must be secured, designed, constructed, commissioned, and ready for technical fit-out. - Integrate land, utility, interconnection, permitting, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and network-readiness schedules into a single capacity view. - Identify capacity gaps, schedule conflicts, stranded-capacity risks, and dependencies that could prevent infrastructure from becoming operational on time. - Develop scenario models comparing self-build, lease, colocation, and strategic development-partner options. - Evaluate delivery pathways based on schedule, cost, control, flexibility, reliability, scalability, and execution risk. - Recommend campus, building, and utility phasing that preserves optionality while supporting near-term deployment requirements. - Assess third-party proposals and determine whether proposed facilities, schedules, technical specifications, and commercial structures can satisfy OpenAI’s requirements. - Partner with capacity planning, energy, real estate, site development, design, construction, commissioning, networking, finance, legal, and commercial teams. - Establish planning assumptions, readiness criteria, decision gates, and governance for moving opportunities from portfolio planning into execution. - Build dashboards and executive-ready materials that communicate capacity supply, demand, timing, assumptions, dependencies, and material risks. - Support investment, build-versus-partner, geographic-prioritization, and portfolio-allocation decisions. - Create repeatable planning frameworks and playbooks that allow OpenAI to scale shell-capacity decisions across regions and infrastructure generations. Qualifications - 8+ years of experience in data center development, infrastructure planning, capacity planning, real estate development, construction planning, program controls, or a related field. - Experience developing or managing portfolio-level plans across multiple data center sites, buildings, or infrastructure programs. - Strong understanding of the data center development lifecycle, including site readiness, power delivery, design, permitting, construction, commissioning, and operational turnover. - Ability to translate technical and demand requirements into facility-capacity, schedule, and phasing decisions. - Strong quantitative and scenario-modeling skills, including the ability to work with incomplete or changing assumptions. - Experience evaluating competing delivery strategies and communicating cost, schedule, flexibility, and risk tradeoffs. - Strong cross-functional program leadership and the ability to create alignment across technical, commercial, and operational organizations. - Excellent written communication and executive-presentation skills. - Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where capacity requirements, technical assumptions, and delivery timelines may change quickly. About the Team
DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike. We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact. We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries. As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries. We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better
About the Role
As a Hardware Engineer, Electronics Packaging & Vehicle Integration, you will lead the mechanical architecture, design, and delivery of electromechanical systems for DoorDash’s next-generation autonomous delivery vehicle. You will develop robust packaging solutions for compute, electrical, communications, and sensor-related hardware that operate reliably in demanding real-world fleet environments.
This role sits at the intersection of mechanical engineering, vehicle integration, and product reliability. You will partner closely with electrical engineering, PCB design, industrial design, systems engineering, manufacturing, supplier partners, reliability, and operations teams to turn system requirements into durable, manufacturable, serviceable, and cost-effective product designs.
You will own designs from concept through launch, including electronic enclosures, housings, mounting systems, seals, connector interfaces, and vehicle-level integration features. Success in this role requires strong mechanical design judgment, practical experience with production processes, and the ability to resolve cross-functional packaging tradeoffs.
Responsibilities:
Own the mechanical design and release of electronic packaging, housings, enclosures, and vehicle integration solutions in support of program timing and product launch.
Design components and assemblies including castings, injection-molded parts, stampings, seals, brackets, PCBA mounts, connector interfaces, and vehicle mounting interfaces.
Create and maintain production-quality 3D CAD and drawings; lead CAD design reviews with cross-functional stakeholders.
Define mechanical requirements and interfaces for electrical, compute, communications, and other electromechanical subsystems.
Perform design calculations, GD&T development, tolerance stack-ups, and other engineering analyses needed to validate design intent.
Develop and execute analysis and test plans for new designs, including proof-of-concept builds, bench testing, and design validation activities.
Partner with electrical engineers and PCB designers to integrate components into reliable, manufacturable electromechanical assemblies.
Lead DFx activities with manufacturing and supplier partners, incorporating design-for-manufacturing, assembly, serviceability, reliability, and cost considerations.
Identify design risks, drive technical tradeoff decisions, and communicate design progress, issues, and mitigation plans to program stakeholders.
Support supplier engagement, prototype builds, root-cause investigations, and continuous product improvement through launch and fleet deployment.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Contribute materially to the form and function of a high profile delivery robot— your work will be on display for all to see and interact with You want to build products that millions of people interact with—not just drive. Every engineering decision directly impacts the customer experience.You're energized by solving first-of-their-kind engineering problems at the intersection of robotics, automotive engineering, and logistics.You enjoy working on products that move quickly from concept to real-world deployment, where engineering decisions immediately translate into operational impact.You believe autonomous delivery has the potential to fundamentally reshape local commerce by making deliveries safer, more sustainable, and more affordable.You're excited to join a highly collaborative team where mechanical engineering plays a central role in defining the future of autonomous last-mile delivery.
We’re excited about you because…
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
6+ years of experience designing electromechanical products, electronics packaging, vehicle systems, robotics, automotive systems, or other ruggedized hardware from concept through production.
Experience packaging compute, electrical, communications, sensor, or power-electronics hardware into mechanically robust assemblies and enclosures.
Strong mechanical design experience with components and processes such as die castings, injection moldings, stampings, extrusions, machined parts, seals, gaskets, brackets, and welded assemblies.
Experience integrating PCBAs, connectors, wire harnesses, cooling solutions, and serviceable electrical interfaces into complete electromechanical systems.
Deep understanding of design for manufacturability, assembly, serviceability, reliability, cost, and supplier capability.
Extensive CAD experience, preferably NX, Team Center, with SolidWorks or CATIA also welcomed; able to create robust parametric models, detailed drawings, and complex assemblies.
Strong command of GD&T, tolerance analysis, stack-ups, datum strategy, and interface definition for assemblies with multiple mechanical and electrical contributors.
Familiarity with structural design, vibration, shock, fatigue, ingress protection, corrosion prevention, and environmental sealing for outdoor or vehicle-mounted products.
Ability to use engineering fundamentals and data to make design decisions; experience with FEA, hand calculations, test data analysis, MATLAB, Python, or similar tools is a plus.
Experience developing and executing design verification plans, proof-of-concept testing, and root-cause investigations.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional technical discussions and resolve packaging tradeoffs across mechanical, electrical, systems, manufacturing, reliability, and operations teams.
Comfortable moving between CAD design reviews, supplier discussions, prototype builds, test execution, and hands-on troubleshooting on the shop floor.
Experience with commercial vehicles, autonomous vehicles, robotics, or other high-duty-cycle fleet products is strongly preferred.

Great Company Culture.
Ranked as one of the most creative and innovative places to work, creativity, innovation, efficiency, diversity and philanthropy are among the core tenets of our organization and are integral drivers of our continued success.
